claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT augmented with DFT+U or hybrid functionals and longitudinal spin fluctuations can reliably identify ferromagnetic ground states in transition-metal materials at low temperature.
The target systems are transition-metal compounds or elemental ferromagnets in a static, near-0 K electronic state.
The proposed method combines spin-polarized DFT, DFT+U or a hybrid functional, and an LSF treatment.
Cryogenic conditions ensure that a static electronic structure is probed.
The proposed calculation accurately treats electron-electron correlations.
The proposed calculation accurately treats spin polarization.
The computed electronic density distribution mediates stabilization of ferromagnetic order.
The computed local-magnetic-moment configuration mediates stabilization of ferromagnetic order.
Advanced exchange-correlation functionals improve the description of magnetic exchange interactions.
Advanced exchange-correlation functionals improve the description of electron correlation.
LSF methods explicitly model thermally excited longitudinal fluctuations of magnetic moments.
Combining advanced functionals with LSF distinguishes the ferromagnetic configuration as lower in energy than competing magnetic orders.
The refined method will predict that the ferromagnetic configuration has lower total energy than non-magnetic and antiferromagnetic configurations.
The refined method will predict well-defined local magnetic moments.
Standard non-spin-polarized calculations fail to capture essential exchange-correlation effects relevant to ferromagnetism.
Simple mean-field models fail to capture essential exchange-correlation effects relevant to ferromagnetism.
The method is most applicable to transition-metal systems with moderate electron correlations.
Strongly correlated systems may require further refinement beyond the proposed method.
The proposed method is expected to improve prediction of ferromagnetic ground states, but its quantitative energy differences remain uncertain.

For an experimentally ferromagnetic material, failure to place the ferromagnetic configuration at the lowest energy or failure to enhance local moments relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The target is described as a static, near-0 K state, while the method's LSF component is justified as explicitly modeling thermal spin fluctuations. The cited LSF evidence concerns finite-temperature paramagnetic states and elevated-temperature properties, so the role of LSF under the stated static near-0 K conditions is internally unresolved.

The baseline is defined as non-spin-polarized calculations and simple mean-field models, but the proposed experiment instead uses standard spin-polarized DFT without advanced corrections as its baseline.
